messages:
maria-support: Escalation from Acme — they report p95 regression only for streaming responses. Non-stream (sync) p95 ~1.8s, streaming p95 ~3.4s. TTFB looks similar across both (~180-220ms). Request IDs: req-ffaa1122, req-ffb3344. Path: POST /v1/stream/generate. Customer sees this across two regions. Can eng/sre take a look?
ops-bot: alert: streaming-p95-spike detected for tenant=acme-prod window=10:02-10:15 UTC — rate +12%, p95 increase +85% :rotating_light:
alex-eng: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro curl and one of the raw response headers for a streaming request? Also include whether client is using SSE or HTTP/2 bidi streams.
maria-support: Repro curl they ran (sanitized):
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream/generate \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini-infer","input":"summarize...","stream":true}'
Client notes: using browser fetch -> EventSource polyfill (SSE). They also tried Node fetch with http2 disabled and saw same.
sam-eng: Is this reproduceable in our internal canary? Is it model-specific? Which model + quantization?
maria-support: Observed with model=gpt-4o-mini-infer (float16), also reported on another small variant. Seen in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
ingrid-sre: Quick hypothesis: proxy/edge coalescing or CDN flush window is delaying chunks after the first one — so TTFB (first chunk) is normal, but backend emits tokens continuously and proxy accumulates then flushes bigger payloads; that increases total time for client to see completion. Need example headers showing Transfer-Encoding and any buffering middleware. Also want backend trace with first_chunk_time_ms and last_token_time_ms.
john-acme: For the sample req-ffaa1122 we measured: non-stream p95=1.82s, streaming p95=3.42s. TTFB measured by client ~210ms for both. We can run more tests on request. :+1:
alex-eng: Can you paste the response headers from the streaming request (include Server, Transfer-Encoding, any x-accel or x-proxy-.* headers)? Also include backend_trace_id (if available).
maria-support: Headers for req-ffaa1122 (sanitized):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: redwood-edge/2.3.1
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
X-Proxy-Coalesce-Window: 500ms
X-Backend-Trace: trace-99321

Log snippet for req-ffaa1122 (from backend):
[trace-99321] first_chunk_ms=210 backend_emit_first_token_ms=200 backend_emit_last_token_ms=1600 total_tokens=145
[trace-99321] backend_model_latency_ms=1600 proxy_coalesce_hold_ms=1300 client_stream_close_ms=3400

sam-eng: That X-Proxy-Coalesce-Window is suspicious — 500ms window + backend model latency ~1600ms means multiple small chunks could be held and then flushed in a few big writes. That would increase perceived completion time.
ingrid-sre: Agreed. Two immediate experiments:
  1) Ask edge team to temporarily set X-Proxy-Coalesce-Window=50ms for acme-prod (or tenant override) and re-run the streaming repro.
  2) Run a non-streaming request and a streaming request with backend configured to emit flush_every=1 (force more frequent small chunk writes) and compare chunk count/size. Use curl -N and tcpdump to verify.
alex-eng: Also instrument and emit: stream_chunk_count, avg_chunk_bytes, and per-request chunk_flush_delay_ms into our tracing so we can build a dashboard. For mitigation plan, we can:
  - Short-term: pin this tenant to non-streaming endpoint or route to dedicated capacity where edge coalesce window is tuned.
  - Medium-term: expose tenant-level coalesce window and add streaming-tail health metrics + alert.
maria-support: Customer is open to a short test window. They can run the test at 11:00 UTC for 10 minutes. I'll coordinate.
john-acme: We'll run a batch of 50 requests streaming+nonstream and provide client-side timings and raw tcp captures.
sam-eng: For the 11:00 window, SRE please enable a temporary tenant override: "coalesce_window_ms=50" + collect response-chunk sizes and timestamps (trace). I can add a temporary metric tag tenant=acme-prod.
ingrid-sre: I'll open an infra change and post the change ID here when done. Also: add a quick patch to the edge to add header X-Early-Flush:true when backend sets flush_every=1 — that should bypass coalescer.
alex-eng: One more quick test: try streaming with HTTP/2 client (no SSE) to see if difference is client-polyfill-related. If SSE polyfill buffers until newline, that could interact with coalescing.
maria-support: Noted. Next steps summary: coordinate 11:00 UTC window, edge override coalesce_window_ms=50, customer will run 50+ paired tests and provide tcpdump + client timings, eng will add temp tracing for chunk counts, SRE to post change-id.
ops-bot: note: incident-created?false refs=streaming-p95-acme-1745008888
maria-support: Thanks all — I'll post results and the customer's raw captures after the run. :eyes:
